title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-prem Deployment Guidelines, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade/Rollback, and Customer Requirements Library
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference guidance for private deployments (VPC and on-prem): an opinionated deployment checklist, reference architectures, packaging recommendations, day-2 operational runbook items, and deterministic upgrade & rollback procedures. The target reader is an SRE/Platform engineer implementing, operating, or validating a private deployment for production LLM inference.

Scope

- Applies to: Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem bundles) deployed by Redwood or by customers using the official on-prem package.
- Excludes: hosted API operational guides, Dedicated (reserved capacity) planning details.

Goals

- Provide a repeatable deployment checklist that maps customer requirements to configuration knobs.
- Describe validated reference architectures for small (1-2 racks), medium (3-10 racks) and large (>10 racks) footprints.
- Define on-prem packaging and installation validation steps.
- Provide Day-2 ops runbook items: monitoring, backups, capacity scaling, incident triage.
- Provide deterministic upgrade and rollback playbooks with safety gates and verification steps.

Prerequisites and Customer Requirements

Short checklist (should be validated before scheduling install):

1. Networking and security
   - Customer provides VPC/subnets or on-prem VLANs with dedicated control plane access.
   - NAT or outbound egress rules to allow image/artifact pulls from our registries (allowed domains: registry.redwood-inference.example, artifacts.redwood-inference.example).
   - VPN or Direct Connect / ExpressRoute for control plane peering if opting for managed control plane.
   - Allowed ports: 22 (maintenance, optional), 443 (control plane), 8070-8085 (internal service endpoints), 3000 (prometheus remote write receiver), 9090 (grafana proxied), 9100-9200 (node exporter/metrics).

2. Hardware & capacity
   - Minimum: 2 GPU nodes (NVIDIA A10/A100 equivalent) + 2 control nodes for HA in small test deployments.
   - Recommended for production: at least 4 GPU nodes + 3 control/infra nodes per cluster.
   - Disk: NVMe local scratch (1-2 TB per GPU node) for KV cache and model shards.
   - Network: 25Gbps recommended for intra-rack; 100Gbps for multi-rack model parallel deployments.

3. Identity & Key Management
   - KMS endpoint for customer-managed keys (if required).
   - Service account with least privilege for provisioning.

4. Compliance
   - Data residency and retention requirements documented and mapped to storage configs (S3-compatible, NFS, or local).

Reference Architectures (high level)

Table: Reference architectures by size

| Profile | GPU Nodes | Control/Infra Nodes | Network | Storage |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| Small (dev/test) | 2 | 2 | 10-25Gbps | Local NVMe + small NFS for artifacts |
| Medium (prod single-rack) | 4-8 | 3 | 25-100Gbps | Per-node NVMe + S3 compatible object store |
| Large (multi-rack) | 10+ | 5+ | 100Gbps fabric + leaf/spine | Distributed object store + networked NVMe caching |

Notes:
- Use RDMA where supported for multi-GPU sharded model serving to reduce latency.
- Separate control plane traffic (control plane subnets) from inference data plane.

On-prem Packaging & Installation

Packaging model: single tarball + Helm charts for Kubernetes deployments, or an offline image bundle for air-gapped on-prem installs. The official package contains:

- images.txt (sha256 list of required container images)
- helm/ (Redwood helm charts, templated for customer values)
- manifests/ (CRDs and manifests for non-K8s installers)
- install.sh (installer wrapper)
- checksums.sig (PGP signature over the bundle)

Installation validation steps (post-install smoke tests):

1. All control plane pods in Running state within 5 minutes.
2. Metrics endpoint available: curl -f https://<control-plane>/healthz returns 200 and version header.
3. Inference runtime can load a small model (resnet32-like test model) and complete an init request in < 30s.
4. KV cache write/read roundtrip latency < 10ms for local NVMe, < 50ms for networked cache.

Configuration snippets (examples)

YAML example for minimal resource allocation (K8s values.yaml excerpt):

```yaml
global:
  cluster_name: "redwood-private-prod"
  registry: "registry.redwood-inference.example"
controller:
  replicas: 3
gpuPool:
  nodeSelector: { "node.kubernetes.io/gpu": "true" }
  resources:
    limits:
      cpu: "16"
      memory: "64Gi"
storage:
  model_store: "s3://customer-model-store"
  cache_local_path: "/var/lib/redwood/cache"
```

Day-2 Operations (runbook items)

Observability
- SLOs:
  - P99 latency (generate endpoint): 600ms target for short prompts (<=128 tokens).
  - Error rate: < 0.5% request failures; 99.9% success for control plane heartbeats per minute.
- Alerts to configure:
  - Node GPU memory pressure > 85% for 5m -> page oncall.
  - Inference queue length > threshold (configured per pool) -> scale signal.
  - Model load failures > 3 within 10 minutes -> alert.

Routine maintenance
1. Weekly: verify backups of model-store metadata and artifact catalog.
2. Monthly: rotate TLS certificates for internal endpoints if using short-lived certs.
3. Quarterly: run full restore drill for artifact storage and control plane.

Scaling & Capacity
- Autoscaling policy recommendations: 60% GPU utilization target for scale-out; 20% target for scale-in cooldown.
- Burst capacity: allow an additional 1-2 nodes for scheduled release windows; configure instance pool warmers to pre-pull images and warm caches.

Incident triage (high level)

1. Symptom: Increased inference latency
   - Check metrics: per-route token latency, queue lengths, GPU utilization.
   - Determine if caused by hot-prefix: inspect cache hit rate.
   - Action: temporarily route traffic to fallback model variant or reduce max_tokens to limit per-request work.
2. Symptom: Model load failures on many nodes
   - Check image and artifact registry reachability, disk space, file permissions.
   - Action: redeploy model loader job on a single node to reproduce; escalate to platform if checksum mismatches.
3. Symptom: Control plane unresponsive
   - Check control plane pod statuses, etcd/DB replication lag, control plane logs.
   - Action: promote standby control node, restore DB from latest consistent snapshot if necessary.

Upgrade and Rollback Procedures

Principles:
- All upgrades must be staged: Canary -> Gradual -> Full.
- Keep a verified rollback artifact for each upgrade.
- Provide safety gates: automated health checks and manual approval windows.

Pre-upgrade checklist:
1. Verify current cluster state is healthy (no degraded pods, SLOs within thresholds for 2 hours).
2. Create a full snapshot of control plane DB and upload to stable artifact store.
3. Snapshot model store metadata and ensure object store versioning is enabled.
4. Identify canary nodes and mark them with label redwood-canary=true.

Upgrade procedure (example sequence):
1. Deploy control plane minor version to canary nodes only.
2. Run smoke tests against canary for 30 minutes (healthz, load small test model, metrics baseline).
3. If canary passes, batch upgrade GPU-node agent + runtime on 10-20% of nodes and wait 15-30 minutes for stability.
4. Evaluate metrics: latency, error rate, model load success, memory/GC.
5. Continue rolling upgrades in batches with a 10-15 minute verification window between batches.
6. After full rollout, run a post-upgrade verification suite (heavy workload simulation, end-to-end latency checks).

Rollback procedure (if upgrade causes regression):
1. Immediately pause the rollout.
2. Revert the updated control plane to previous image/manifest on nodes labeled redwood-canary and re-run smoke tests.
3. If canary reverts successfully, trigger cohort rollback for all upgraded nodes in parallel batches, using the preserved previous images.
4. Restore DB from snapshot only if data corruption is detected (and after engineering approval).
5. Post-rollback: collect logs, capture heap/core dumps for root cause analysis and create an incident review.

Safety checks and automation tips

- Keep at least two historical control plane snapshots for last 72 hours.
- Automate smoke tests using our CI-runner image: redwood/upgrade-smoke:stable.
- Use feature flags for risky model-serving changes (gradual activation per route).

Customer Requirements Library (mapping of common asks to config choices)

Table: Requirements -> Recommended config option

| Requirement | Recommended config | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Minimize inference latency | Use local NVMe cache + 100Gbps fabric + RDMA | Avoid networked model store for hot models |
| Data residency | Configure object store endpoint in customer region + local NVMe | Enable object store encryption at rest |
| Air-gapped install | Use offline image bundle + signed checksums | Provide PGP key to customer for signature verification |
| FIPS / HSM key management | Integrate with customer HSM via KMS plugin | Validate KMS rotation policy in pre-install checklist |

Appendix: Example CLI checks and commands

- Check pod health (K8s): kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide
- Fetch control plane health: curl -sS -H '"Authorization: Bearer <token>"' https://<control-plane>/api/v1/health | jq .
- Verify model load: curl -sS -X POST https://<gateway>/v1/models/test-model:predict -d '{"input":"hello"}' | jq .

Common troubleshooting commands

- Check disk usage: ssh node && sudo du -sh /var/lib/redwood/cache/*
- GPU memory overview: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
